architecture.goal: Implement a simple and defendable end-to-end flow for the challenge core by using a daily producer, SQS FIFO for provider serialization, a direct consumer for provider execution, and DynamoDB for final outcomes.
runtime_shape: EventBridge Scheduler triggers Producer Lambda once per day
Producer Lambda resolves target date and reads pending records for that date
Producer Lambda publishes one SQS FIFO message per eligible pending record
SQS FIFO enforces provider-level ordering through MessageGroupId
Consumer Lambda reads SQS messages and executes provider API calls directly
Consumer Lambda persists success outcomes or terminal failure outcomes in the results table
explicit_non_goals_for_phase: Pending-record lifecycle state transitions beyond PENDING

module_boundaries.responsibility: Start the daily core flow and optionally pass a target-date override.
Read pending records for a target date and dispatch one FIFO message per eligible record.
Preserve same-provider ordering and enable cross-provider concurrency.
Execute the provider request for one record and persist the final outcome.
Store successful outcomes and terminal failures in a durable and auditable structure.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: ProviderRecord
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Represent one pending work item to be executed.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: SqsMessage
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Transport one ProviderRecord through FIFO queueing.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: FailureResult
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Represent a terminal provider failure stored as a final outcome.

data_and_storage_design.decision: Keep a table that supports reading pending records for a target date in phase 1.
data_and_storage_design.usage: The producer reads items whose logical date matches the execution date and whose status is PENDING.
data_and_storage_design.note: Phase 1 accepts the current date-based access pattern as a temporary core-flow baseline, even though phase 3 will revisit large-scale partitioning.

data_and_storage_design.decision: Store one final outcome record per processed item, whether success or terminal failure.
data_and_storage_design.usage: The consumer writes auditable outcome records keyed by provider and processed timestamp.
data_and_storage_design.note: Outcome persistence is the authoritative evidence of what happened in phase 1; pending item state transitions are deferred.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Remove orchestrator and Step Functions from the phase 1 runtime path.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: They add complexity that is not needed to demonstrate the core orchestration behavior and make the narrative harder to explain.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Keep pending records selected by status=PENDING only.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: This phase models pending items as inputs, not as a full workflow state machine.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Persist final outcomes instead of mutating pending records through multiple lifecycle states.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: This cleanly separates input eligibility from execution result and avoids premature complexity before phase 2.

behavioral_decisions.decision: Treat terminal errors as persisted failures and non-terminal concerns as future phase work.
behavioral_decisions.rationale: Phase 1 needs deterministic final outcomes for the core path, not complete operational recovery.

changes: Use the scheduled producer as the single entrypoint for daily orchestration.
Wire SQS FIFO directly to the consumer for message execution.
Make the consumer responsible for calling the provider and persisting final outcomes.
Keep producer and consumer domain logic isolated from AWS SDK details through ports and adapters.
Remove or retire the orchestrator path from the core runtime design.
Avoid duplicate mental models for consumer entrypoints; one runtime path should represent the phase 1 design clearly.
CDK must provision only the services used by the phase 1 runtime path.
Queue permissions and lambda event source wiring must match the simplified flow.
Scheduler target, queue target, and table permissions must remain least-privilege and explainable.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: No pending records exist for the target date
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Producer completes successfully without dispatching messages.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: A pending item is not in PENDING state when read
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Producer skips it and counts it as non-dispatched.
Treat the message as failed for the queue-consumer contract and do not persist a synthetic success.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Provider call fails with a terminal error
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Persist a terminal failure outcome record.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Provider call fails with a transient or unexpected error
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Do not solve full retry orchestration in phase 1; preserve error classification in the domain so phase 2 can extend it cleanly.

quality_gates: Producer unit tests validate selection, dispatch, grouping, deduplication, and empty-input behavior.
Consumer unit tests validate success persistence and terminal-failure persistence.
Handler tests validate scheduled input parsing and queue-consumer message handling.
Core phase tests make the end-to-end control flow understandable from scheduler to persistence.
expected_test_scenarios: Producer dispatches one message per pending record.
Consumer persists success outcome on successful provider response.
Consumer persists failure outcome on terminal provider error.
Consumer does not persist success on invalid or terminal execution path.
Queue handler reports failures for invalid or failed messages.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Deliver the minimum correct orchestration flow for the challenge.
tasks: Simplify the runtime architecture to Scheduler -> Producer -> SQS FIFO -> Consumer -> Results Table.
Align domain contracts and adapters with that simplified flow.
Remove or isolate orchestrator and Step Functions from phase 1 runtime responsibilities.
Ensure CDK reflects the simplified runtime design.
Run build and tests and close phase 1 gaps.
definition_of_done: One clear daily orchestration path exists.
Provider-level serialization is enforced by queue configuration and message grouping.
Success and terminal failure outcomes are persisted.
The simplified architecture is reflected consistently in code, tests, and CDK.

assumptions: The current repository may reuse existing producer and consumer domain pieces where they align with the simplified design.
Transient-error retry behavior can remain intentionally incomplete in phase 1 as long as the classification boundary stays explicit for later phases.
Date-based pending-record access is acceptable as a temporary phase-1 simplification even though it is not the final large-scale answer.
